_: THE ONE HOME for shipped-record versions. A version here is raised BY HAND, and raising it is
what redelivers a record to every install. Nothing raises it automatically and nothing derives
it from content — see the argument below.
WHY A VERSION AND NOT A CONTENT COMPARISON. The moment an operator edits a record their copy
differs from the seed. A content comparison would therefore overwrite and warn on every boot,
forever, on every install that has ever been used. The version is the only thing that can say
WE MEANT THIS, and it has to be said deliberately.
WHY A SIDECAR AND NOT A FIELD INSIDE THE RECORD. Four reasons, in order of weight:
1. A record field is WRITABLE BY AN OPERATOR EDIT. PUT /api/tracks/:id builds the stored
record as { ...existing, ...req.body }, so any field the body carries lands unvalidated;
the handler re-pins id, isDefault, backgroundImageFile and createdAt by name precisely
because that spread does not protect anything it is not told to protect. An export/import
round-trip or an editor replaying a record from another install would move the version by
accident. Out here, nothing an operator can reach through the app writes it.
2. BINARIES HAVE NO INSIDE. A background jpg and a logo cannot carry a field, so they need a
sidecar whatever tracks do. One form everywhere beats two forms and a rule about which.
3. THE UNIT IS THE THING VERSIONED, not the file. A track ships WITH its background and a
brand WITH its logo, as the owner set the scope. A field inside the track JSON has nowhere
to say that and nowhere to put the background half.
4. ONE PLACE TO RAISE AND ONE PLACE TO CHECK. A human raising a version edits this file; the
guard reads this file. Twelve versions in twelve records is twelve places to forget.
HOW DELIVERY READS IT (server/src/seedDelivery.js owns the behaviour, not this comment):
shipped version HIGHER than what the install recorded -> the whole unit is overwritten and
the operator is warned. EQUAL, LOWER, ABSENT or not an integer -> nothing happens. Silence is
the safe default; delivery is the exception that has to be asked for.
A RECORD WITH NO UNIT HERE IS NEVER A TARGET. Delivery walks this manifest, so an operator own
creation cannot be reached by it — not by a filter that could be got wrong, but because the
loop never visits it.
TO REDELIVER A RECORD: change its files, raise its version by one here, commit both together.
scripts/check-seed-versions.mjs FAILS the commit if you change the files and forget the version.
